## FINDING: exact Gaussian scalar admission of PR[3577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3577)'s fixed kernel direction

For the particular direction identified in [PR3577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3577), allowing Gaussian integer rescaling does not improve on the factor-four control: its exact scalar admission ideal is **$4\mathbb Z[i]$**.

This finding fixes the [published source head `33997335997f1eef37ee4f455244cd289ba07b06`](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/tree/33997335997f1eef37ee4f455244cd289ba07b06/research/p104-kernel-consumer). Let $R=\mathbb Z[i]$, $\pi=1+i$, and let $p$ be exactly its prepared field from the PR[3467](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3467) coefficient $a_{44}=\delta_{15}$. Initialise the unchanged 5,398-event WORD by

$$
Y91=\lambda p,\qquad Y90=-\lambda p,\qquad \lambda\in R,
$$

with all other 356 initial public banks zero. Require every fractional ADD increment to be Gaussian integral and every completed signed-floor native pair to equal its ideal Gaussian $C$ pair. In exact-integer semantics, the whole word meets this contract **if and only if**

$$
\lambda\in4R=\pi^4R.
$$

Zero is included. Rounded native executions remain outside this exactness contract; their integer floor outputs are not asserted to be undefined.

### Three necessary witnesses and one sufficient generator

All indices are zero-based.

| Scalar class | First exactness failure | Actual source-bound witness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $v_\pi(\lambda)=0$ or $1$ | Event 1099: `D1 += Y90/4`, frame `[381,241,2]` | Address 10 has donor $-2\lambda$, requiring increment $-\lambda/2$. |
| $v_\pi(\lambda)=2$ | Event 1101: rank-one D1 native | For $\lambda=2$, bit 0/address 4 has input $(0,i)$ and twice-ideal outputs $(1+i,-1+i)$. |
| $v_\pi(\lambda)=3$ | Event 2120: rank-seven private-C native | For $\lambda=2+2i$, bit 2/address 0 has input $(i,0)$ and twice-ideal outputs $(-1+i,1+i)$. |

Here is the universal implication behind those finite checks. The literal pair agrees with $C$ whenever the latter's outputs are Gaussian integral: writing $d=a-b$, integrality makes the real and imaginary components of $d$ have the same parity, so the floor differences equal their exact half differences. Thus multiplying an **already exact** prefix by any $\mu\in R$ preserves exactness. This does not assume homogeneity of rounded execution.

The retained $p$ trace passes the prefix before 1099, so that read forces $\lambda=2\mu$. The new $2p$ trace then passes up to its displayed 1101 pair. Its scaled ideal outputs are $\mu(1+i)/2$ and $\mu(-1+i)/2$, integral precisely when $\mu\in\pi R$. Write $\lambda=2\pi\nu$. The new $(2+2i)p$ trace passes up to the displayed 2120 pair, including its earlier native directions; that pair forces $\nu\in\pi R$. Hence $\lambda\in2\pi^2R=4R$.

Conversely, the retained complete $4p$ trace checks all 5,398 events, every active completed native pair, and all eight private zero erasures. For $\lambda=4\mu$, multiply each of its states by $\mu$. Exact fractional increments and ideal native outputs remain Gaussian integral, the literal-pair lemma applies at every pair, and zero erasures remain zero. This proves sufficiency for the entire scalar ideal without a new universal Clifford-covariance assumption or a broad source-module census.

### Completed B9 membership and physical returns

Demanding B9 membership at every completed event gives the same scalar ideal, but an earlier distinction is visible. Immediately after event 1099, the **unnormalised** degree-two Möbius/Newton coefficient at mask 10 is $-\lambda/2$. B9 requires divisibility by $\pi^2$, forcing $\lambda\in4R$. Both $2p$ and $(2+2i)p$ therefore leave B9 at 1099; their raw coefficients are respectively $-1$ and $-1-i$. The second still executes exact Gaussian native arithmetic until 2120. This is a completed-field assertion, not a claim about every internal temporary.

For admitted scalars, PR[3577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3577)'s physical endpoint remains

$$
\rho_5(y)=0,\qquad X0_{\rm final}=J_F(-\lambda p/2),
$$

including the late sign at event 5086. The Y sources still end in their declared dimension-eight frames. Scaling supplies neither a two-role preparation from one upstream source nor an entrance-frame return for a borrowed source. Actual source access/preparation, adapters, owners, control, finite widths and the complete supplier allowance remain obligations. Arbitrarily large $\lambda$ in the mathematical statement does not imply one fixed finite-width implementation.
